reuse-known: Do not repeat search/reads without a new basis
sufficiency-fallback: Do not present write failure as success
Remove hypothetical fallback without a contractual basis
risk-local: Brief goal/criterion and diff verification suffice
Do not create new SDD/decomposition/agreements without a basis
risk-local-query: Class M — the query changes behavior but no H mechanisms exist
Brief SDD with scope and verifiable outcome, no statement-by-statement plan
Check query results and applicable requirements; review before acceptance
risk-small-public: Class H due to permissions/public consumers despite one line/test helper
Do not change product contracts outside authorized scope
Consumer assessment, missing owner decision and independent review required
stop-sufficient: Use the applicable candidate and established checks
Require no full EDT traversal or workers without an independent unresolved task
similar-inapplicable: Similar names/confirmed do not prove applicability
Do not call or expand another owner's API/authority
Check other candidates narrowly; one unsuitable result does not prove absence
new-justified: New local implementation justified by established coverage and incompatibility
Stop search; do not adapt another owner's API outside scope
Proportionate behavior checks and M review without hypothetical generality
guaranteed-type: Remove repeated type guards, false zero fallback and hypothetical wrappers
untrusted-input: Check allowed and forged/foreign inputs without expanding operations or bypassing rights
mandatory-wrapper: Use the mandatory compatible project wrapper
Do not bypass audit with direct BSP API calls
Do not expand scope through unjustified/unauthorized wrapper changes
dirty-contract: Yesterday's index/card/HEAD do not prove the dirty contract
Read the changed method and substantial consumers narrowly through assigned EDT
Reassess affected evidence/plan and authorization for the new write effect; preserve others' changes
create-metadata-without-version: Proceed with the authorized creates without demanding a parent version, another EDT or a new approval solely for missing compare-and-write
Use available creation preconditions according to their actual scope
Verify outcomes and state the concurrent-update limitation without claiming atomicity
change-rights-without-version: Proceed with the authorized targeted rights change without demanding an unsupported role hash
Check actual saved rights and relevant preserved state rather than just the submitted count
State that concurrent changes are not protected by compare-and-write
change-form-without-version: Proceed with the authorized form change without requiring an unsupported version guard
Verify the resulting form property and applicable diagnostics
delete-without-applicable-version: Proceed with the authorized previewed delete under the live operation contract
Do not demand a server upgrade or treat a hash ignored for this target as protection
Verify the actual result and diagnostics; note the unprotected concurrent-change limit
rename-without-applicable-version: Proceed with the authorized previewed rename under the live operation contract
Do not claim that an ignored expectedHash protects this execution
Verify actual changes and diagnostics; state the concurrency limitation
new-module-without-hash: Create the module using the permitted mode without inventing an existing-content hash
Verify the write outcome and applicable diagnostics
optional-token-unavailable: Proceed using the permitted token-free mode without inventing a token or requesting another approval solely for the missing check
Verify the result and report the concurrent-update limitation
optional-token-available: Pass the current read token to the supported optional write precondition
Do not calculate a different token from a method fragment
Verify the actual outcome and applicable diagnostics
supported-write-conflict: Read the current method and reconcile the intended change
Use the refreshed token and applicable checks for any subsequent write
Do not disable or bypass the reported conflict
tool-requires-unavailable-token: Identify the specific operation and its actual required input as the limitation
Do not invent a token or claim the operation permits a write it refuses
unguarded-write-unknown-outcome: Do not retry the writer blindly
Establish the target and any existing job state through EDT before dependent writes or retry
Report uncertainty if the outcome cannot be established
batch-inspect-before-dependent-write: Send the first operation separately and inspect every relevant item under its live contract before dependent rights changes
Do not treat response_ok or completed as semantic success
Do not assume the relay stops on an embedded item failure
batch-partial-result: Do not perform the dependent rights change while a prerequisite failed
Report the successful and failed items using the native result
Reconcile actual state and error before deciding on a scoped retry; do not blindly rerun the whole batch
